description_full: Cadeler plc, together with its subsidiaries, operates as an offshore wind installation vessel contractor in Denmark, the United Kingdom, Germany, Poland, rest of Europe, the United States, and Taiwan. The company engages in the transport and installation of offshore wind turbine generators, foundations, and topsides and substations; maintenance of offshore wind turbine generators, and offshore structures and platforms; and offshore construction within renewable space. It also involved offshore decommissioning within renewable space; salvage assistance; and heavy lift and project cargo. In addition, the company owns and operates ten offshore jack-up windfarm installation vessels. Further, it also provides hydraulic pile driving solutions. Cadeler plc was incorporated in 2008 and is based in Norwich, United Kingdom.

culture_narrative: Employs approximately 1K people. Revenue per employee of $608K ranks in the top quartile among Industrials peers. Stock-based compensation of $2K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 4× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity).
financial_summary: Cadeler plc is a mid-cap industrials business with a $2.4B market cap on $684M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +84% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 6% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 52% confirm genuine pricing power.
The company is burning through $930M of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 3.5× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage of 14× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield is only 0.1%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 31% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 4.5× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.01 across 548 companies in the universe; the top four hold 9% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted higher, up 17% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 69% over the last three months.
The price sits near the bottom of its 52-week range, 80% below the high.

At current returns, reinvesting 100% of profits supports about 5.8% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
